survivors.claim: serveAtlas's timeout path now waits unboundedly on the child's 'exit' event before rejecting, so if the SIGKILL ever fails to take (or is regressed away) the promise never settles; the AC-20260909-06-4 pin's red is then an indefinite hang rather than a failure, because Node 26 does not fire the test's own { timeout: 6000 } on a never-settling promise and the repo's test runner sets no --test-timeout/--test-force-exit.
survivors.impact: The regression this test guards against would show up as the whole test run stalling forever instead of a red test, which is the exact hang class the port work set out to eliminate.
survivors.evidence: Kill-removed falsification (spawn patched so kill('SIGKILL') is a no-op, shipped assertions verbatim): no test line printed; a 20 s watchdog fired with 'stub alive=true', exit 99. Per-test timeout probe: test with { timeout: 500 } awaiting a never-settling promise did not time out in 5 s. package.json test script carries no timeout flag; grep for test-timeout|force-exit across .claude, spec/scripts, scripts exits 1. test-file-budget-reporter.js fires only from summed per-file durations after the file ends. The same falsified file under --test-timeout=8000 --test-force-exit fails cleanly at 8001 ms. Fix shape: race the exit wait against a short grace (e.g. 1000 ms) and reject with err.child attached either way, so the shipped exitCode/signalCode assertion fails within a bound instead of hanging.
